title: Anthropic continues compute-gobbling streak in $45B deal with Nscale
content:
Anthropic has signed a deal to rent about $45 billion in AI compute from Nscale, a British AI infrastructure company, a source familiar with the deal told TechCrunch.
Nscale, founded only in 2024, has already cut deals with the likes of Microsoft and will supply Anthropic with compute via Nvidia’s Vera Rubin chips, its new state-of-the-art chip system.
The Vera Rubin system combines six different chips working in concert and is considered the cutting edge of chip design. The compute capacity is expected to start powering the AI lab’s services in late 2027, the source said.
The deal, first reported by Bloomberg, is only the latest in a spree of compute partnerships for Anthropic. Bloomberg writes that the deal spans six years, with the computing power coming from Nscale’s flagship data center in West Virginia.
Over the past eight months, Anthropic has aggressively scaled up its compute capacity in an effort to better compete with rivals, most notably OpenAI.
Earlier this month, Anthropic signed a $10 billion deal with AI cloud startup Volta — founded in January — securing a six-year supply of cloud computing power from a data center in Norway. In July, the company also signed a $5 billion compute-related deal with AMD.
A few months before that, in May, Anthropic revealed it had entered into a large computing deal with SpaceX (run by Elon Musk, whose rivalry with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has made him an unlikely ally of Anthropic). That deal draws computing capacity from two different SpaceX data centers and is reportedly providing Anthropic with $1.25 billion worth of capacity each month.
In April, Anthropic also signed a deal to significantly expand its partnership with Amazon, gaining access to an additional 5 gigawatts of compute. That same month, the company also expanded its relationship with Google and Broadcom, adding even more power capacity.
Anthropic is hardly alone in its enthusiastic pursuit of more AI horsepower. The race to gobble up as much compute capacity as possible is ongoing, with other major players — including Google, OpenAI, and Meta — all following a similar track.

report.summary: Anthropic signs $45 billion compute deal with Nscale, continuing aggressive infrastructure buildup to compete with OpenAI.
report.background: Anthropic's latest $45 billion contract with British AI infrastructure firm Nscale extends a months-long spending spree on compute capacity. Founded in 2024, Nscale has quickly attracted major clients and will supply Anthropic with Nvidia's Vera Rubin systems—a six-chip architecture considered cutting-edge—from its West Virginia data center starting in late 2027. The deal is part of a broader pattern: earlier in 2026, Anthropic committed $10 billion to Volta, $5 billion to AMD, and expanded existing agreements with Amazon, Google, and Broadcom. These moves reflect an industry-wide race, as OpenAI, Google, and Meta also scramble to secure scarce AI compute. Anthropic's strategy leverages diversified suppliers to avoid dependence on any single cloud provider, while positioning itself to train and deploy increasingly powerful frontier models. The scale suggests AI labs now view compute procurement as a core strategic function, not merely an operational cost.
key_points: Anthropic has committed roughly $45 billion to rent AI compute from Nscale, a two-year-old British infrastructure provider backed by Nvidia's latest Vera Rubin chips. The six-year deal is scheduled to begin powering services in late 2027, signaling long-term bets on next-generation hardware.

Nscale is an unusually young supplier, founded in 2024, yet already counts Microsoft as a client. Its flagship West Virginia data center will host the compute, illustrating how quickly new infrastructure players are entering the AI market to meet explosive demand.

This deal extends Anthropic's compute procurement spree: over eight months, it signed a $10 billion agreement with cloud startup Volta, a $5 billion AMD deal, a huge SpaceX arrangement reportedly worth $1.25 billion monthly, plus expanded capacity from Amazon, Google, and Broadcom.

The partnership with SpaceX, run by Elon Musk, is notable given Musk's rivalry with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, making Musk an uneasy ally for Anthropic. It adds political and competitive intrigue to what is otherwise a pure infrastructure transaction.

Anthropic is not alone—Google, OpenAI, and Meta are all stockpiling compute. The race suggests that access to massive clusters is now a primary competitive barrier, and those who secure capacity early may dominate the next generation of AI models.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this deal reinforces a paradigm where compute procurement is as important as research breakthroughs. Anthropic is effectively pre-committing tens of billions over the next several years, which could strain cash flow but secure the raw capacity needed for large-scale training. Developers may benefit from more reliable uptime and newer hardware, though costs will likely be passed down through API pricing. Regular users will see more capable models, but also growing concentration: only a handful of labs can afford these contracts. Smaller startups face a widening gap, while infrastructure providers like Nscale gain leverage. The reliance on Vera Rubin suggests Nvidia's roadmap remains central to AI advancement, and any delays could ripple across Anthropic's timeline.
report.tools: For readers tracking compute infrastructure trends, watch Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform and Nscale's public announcements. Tools like HPC Wire or The Next Platform cover data center deals. Open-source monitoring tools such as Prometheus and Grafana help visualize cluster usage if you're experimenting with distributed training, while Ray is a useful framework for scaling compute-intensive AI workloads across multiple nodes.
